correctness.rationale: The non-leading zero runs of a positive suffix r are unchanged in the concatenation of the digits of q with the padded length-m suffix. Hence any accepted longer index with that suffix has b_r=1; q=0 and r=0 are covered separately by equality and b_0=1. A shifted dyadic window uses the complementary offset sets of two aligned blocks, so summing the coordinatewise bound gives the initial weight as the maximum. After the first binary 1, admissible strings are uniquely tiled by 1 and 00, giving F_l for positive l-digit indices and 1+sum_{l=1}^m F_l=F_{m+2} including index zero and m=0. The binary prefix 101 at every index in [5*2^m,6*2^m) produces an all-zero window. Unit shifts change the weight by at most one and so realize every intermediate Parikh weight. The proof covers all positions and exponents; the supplied finite verification is corroboration only.
